title: Why transportation networks are especially vulnerable to ransomware
主要内容: Transportation networks are especially vulnerable to ransomware attacks due to the high susceptibility of workers to phishing emails. A ransomware attack on San Francisco's light rail system over the Thanksgiving weekend highlighted the impact cybercriminals can have on municipal transportation systems. The attack occurred because a worker invited hackers in by clicking on a malicious link or email attachment, which can quickly spread the virus if the network is interconnected. Ransomware is expected to be a $1 billion cybercriminal business in 2016, according to the FBI. PhishMe's 2016 report found that transportation workers were more likely to open phishing emails than workers in other industries, with about 22% falling for the test scenario. Education workers had the highest susceptibility at 28%, while the average across all industries was 17%. The FBI recommends not paying the ransom, as the San Francisco agency was able to do due to its system backups. Many organizations, especially underfunded government agencies, are not well-prepared for such attacks. PhishMe CEO Rohyt Belani emphasized the importance of frequent backups, updated security software, and employee training to detect suspicious emails. Transportation networks are especially vulnerable to ransomware due to the increasing integration of internet-connected devices. Cybersecurity experts warn that as more devices become part of the internet of things, ransomware attacks could target critical infrastructure such as vehicles and medical devices like pacemakers. Ben Johnson, chief security strategist at Carbon Black, highlights the merging of physical and cyber security, emphasizing that when human safety is at risk, there is greater public awareness and response. This convergence underscores the growing threat of ransomware in the transportation sector and beyond.
